mainTopic: Why the case of a mother raped by one's father (אמו אנוסת אביו) is missing from the משנה: רב אדא קרחינא's and רב אשי's explanations, and לוי's ברייתא
overview: The amud opens with a memory aid that closes the earlier discussion. That discussion showed that רבי חייא's rules fit every case in the משנה, even according to רבי שמעון. The גמרא then asks how to explain רבי's sharp answer to לוי, who wanted to add the case of a mother raped by one's father. רב אדא קרחינא, quoting רבא, says רבי accepts the rules, and this case never fits two of them at once. He shows this with two sisters and with two unrelated women. רב אשי says instead that רבי does not hold of the rules. In his view the משניות follow רבי יהודה, who forbids a woman raped by one's father to all the brothers, and he proves this from the next משנה's list of six severe women. רבינא and רב אשי then suggest cases where she could still fall to her son. The answers are that the משנה does not list cases that need a forbidden marriage or a ממזר brother. Finally, the גמרא notes that לוי still included 'his mother' in his own ברייתא and begins quoting it.

steps.title: A memory aid: died, was born, did יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short mnemonic to remember the case where 'forbidden to this brother, permitted to that brother' works even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And your memory aid is: died, was born, did יבום. Died, was born, did יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier discussion with a short memory aid. It helps you remember a case where one woman is forbidden to one brother but permitted to another, even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One brother died, then a new brother was born, then a living brother did יבום with the widow. This happens twice, with two different deaths, two births and two יבומים. Each newborn brother is forbidden to one widow, as אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, but permitted to the other widow, so the rule 'האסורה לזה מותרת לזה' fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Your sign, a memory aid
He did יבום, marrying his dead brother's childless widow
Was born

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is only a short code to help you remember the long case from the previous discussion.

phrases.english: And your memory aid: died, was born, and did yibum.
phrases.notes: One brother dies, a new brother is born, then another brother marries the widow.

phrases.english: Died, was born, and did yibum.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion (from the earlier part of the daf), which showed that רבי חייא's rules work even according to רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a real case where each widow is forbidden to one brother and permitted to the other, even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Suggestion: רבי does not accept these rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי simply does not hold of רבי חייא's general rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי does not hold of these general rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier discussion has made it hard to explain רבי's view. So the גמרא suggests a simple way out: רבי does not accept רבי חייא's rules at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי חייא's rules apply to every case in the משנה, even according to רבי שמעון, they cause a problem for רבי's position. The easiest fix is to say רבי never agreed to those rules. In the next step, רב אדא קרחינא, quoting רבא, offers a different explanation in which רבי does accept them.

keyTerms.meaning: General rules, here the rules of רבי חייא
He does not hold of it

phrases.english: Rather, according to Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: he does not hold of these general rules.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the difficulty built up in the previous discussion about רבי's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise: רבי does not accept the rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי agrees with רבי חייא's rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps רבי does not hold of them at all.

steps.title: רבי does accept the rules, but the mother case fits only one at a time
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא קרחינא, quoting רבא, says רבי does accept the rules. He told לוי that the case of a mother raped by one's father can fit only one rule, never two at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא קרחינא, sitting before רב כהנא, said in the name of רבא: Really, רבי does hold of these rules. This is what he told לוי: 'his mother who was raped by his father' can be found fitting one rule, but not fitting two.
steps.whatsHappening: A different answer is given. רבי does accept רבי חייא's rules, and that is exactly why he did not add the 'mother raped by his father' case that לוי asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case in the משנה has to fit several of רבי חייא's rules at once. The case of אמו אנוסת אביו can only fit one rule in any given scenario, never two together. So it does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact. It brings us back to the original assumption.
His mother, a woman his father raped and did not marry
You can find it, meaning it can happen
In one, meaning with one rule
In two, meaning with two rules at once

steps.confusionAlert: 'One' and 'two' here are about rules, not women. The case can fit one of רבי חייא's rules, but never two of them in the same scenario.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the case was left out of the משנה without rejecting רבי חייא's rules.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא קַרְחִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
phrases.english: Rav Adda Karchina, before Rav Kahana,
said in the name of Rava:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי,
phrases.english: Really, Rabbi does hold of these general rules,
and this is what he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'To him' means to לוי, who asked רבי why this case wasn't listed.

phrases.english: his mother who was raped by his father —
you can find it with one,
you cannot find it with two.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 2 and offers a different explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: it fits only one rule at a time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either רבי rejects the rules, or the mother case should be on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי keeps the rules. The mother case is left out because it never fits two of them together.

steps.title: If the father raped two sisters
steps.stepSummary: With two sisters, 'אחותה שהיא יבמתה' works, but 'האסורה לזה מותרת לזה' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If יעקב raped two sisters, 'her sister who is her יבמה' can happen, but 'the one forbidden to this brother is permitted to that brother' cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the claim in step 3 with a first scenario. A father raped two sisters, each had a son, and the two women later married two other sons of the father, who then died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both widows are sisters and both are יבמות, so 'אחותה שהיא יבמתה' fits. But each son is forbidden to his own mother and also to his mother's sister. So both women are forbidden to both sons, and 'האסורה לזה מותרת לזה' fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Raped
Her sister who is also her יבמה. Two sisters fall to the same family for יבום.
The woman forbidden to this brother is permitted to that brother

phrases.english: If Yaakov raped two sisters,
phrases.notes: 'יעקב' is just a sample name for the father in this case.

phrases.english: 'her sister who is her yevamah' — you can find it,

phrases.aramaic: הָאֲסוּרָה לָזֶה מוּתֶּרֶת לָזֶה — לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ.
phrases.english: 'forbidden to this one, permitted to that one' — you cannot find it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of step 3's claim with a concrete case.
steps.terutzMaskana: With sisters, only one rule fits.

steps.title: If the father raped two unrelated women
steps.stepSummary: With two unrelated women, 'האסורה לזה מותרת לזה' works, but 'אחותה שהיא יבמתה' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he raped two unrelated women, 'the one forbidden to this brother is permitted to that brother' can happen, but 'her sister who is her יבמה' cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second scenario: the father raped two unrelated women. Now the opposite rule works, which completes the proof that this case never fits two rules at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each woman is forbidden only to her own son as his mother, and she is permitted to the other son, so 'האסורה לזה מותרת לזה' fits. But the women are not sisters, so 'אחותה שהיא יבמתה' fails. In each scenario only one rule fits, so רבי rightly left the case out of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unrelated women, not related to each other

steps.whatToRemember: רבי accepts רבי חייא's rules. 'His mother raped by his father' is not in the משנה because it fits only one rule at a time. With two sisters only 'אחותה שהיא יבמתה' fits. With two unrelated women only 'האסורה לזה מותרת לזה' fits.
steps.confusionAlert: Here נכריות does not mean non-Jewish women. It means women who are strangers to each other, not sisters.

phrases.english: And if he raped two unrelated women,

phrases.aramaic: הָאֲסוּרָה לָזֶה מוּתֶּרֶת לָזֶה — מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ,
phrases.english: 'forbidden to this one, permitted to that one' — you can find it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוֹתָהּ שֶׁהִיא יְבִמְתָּהּ — לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ.
phrases.english: 'her sister who is her yevamah' — you cannot find it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 4. It completes the proof of step 3.
steps.terutzMaskana: With unrelated women, only the other rule fits. So the case never fits two rules together.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of אמו אנוסת אביו is left out of the משנה because it never fits two of רבי חייא's rules at once.

steps.title: רב אשי: רבי does not hold of these rules after all
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי goes back to the idea that רבי does not accept רבי חייא's general rules, and adds that the משנה does deal with disputed cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, רבי does not hold of these general rules, and the משנה does deal with cases that are in dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different answer from רב אדא קרחינא's. He says רבי does not accept רבי חייא's rules, and the משנה can include cases that are argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא קרחינא said רבי does accept the rules. רב אשי returns to the earlier idea that he does not. He also adds a new point: the משנה does follow one side of a dispute. As the next steps show, it follows רבי יהודה, and that is exactly why the case was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (the earlier idea was right after all)
General rules (here, רבי חייא's rules)
A dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי,
phrases.english: Actually, Rabbi does not hold of these general rules,
and the mishnah does deal with disputed cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי הָנֵי כְּלָלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב אדא קרחינא's (steps 3-5), going back to the approach of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי accepts רבי חייא's rules and only meant that one case cannot fit two rules at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי does not accept those rules, and the משנה can include disputed cases.

steps.title: Then what did רבי's harsh words mean?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי doesn't hold of the rules, the גמרא asks what he meant when he said לוי 'has no brain in his head.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what then is 'It seems to me that he has no brain in his head,' which רבי said to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. If רב אשי is right, we need a new reading of רבי's sharp reply to לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי's words were explained as rejecting לוי's question on the basis of the rules. Now that the rules are gone, his reply needs a different meaning. The next step gives it.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems to me
A brain in his head (a sharp put-down)

phrases.english: And what is "It seems to me
that he has no brain in his head"
that he said to him?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי, and 'him' is לוי, who had asked why the woman raped by one's father was missing from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי כִּמְדוּמֶּה אֲנִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מוֹחַ בְּקׇדְקֳדוֹ דְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רב אשי's approach explains רבי's words to לוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי meant by his harsh reply, if not a rejection based on the general rules.

steps.title: רבי meant: read the משנה carefully, it follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי told לוי he should have seen that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids אנוסת אביו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he said to him: Why didn't you read the משנה carefully? The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids a woman raped by one's father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי's words. He was criticizing לוי for not reading the משנה closely enough to see that it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not a general rule but a specific reading of the משנה. Since the משנה follows רבי יהודה, the woman raped by one's father belongs in a different list, so of course she is missing from this one. The proof comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: You read closely / carefully
A woman raped by one's father

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
Why did you not read the mishnah carefully?
For the mishnah follows Rabbi Yehuda
who forbids a woman raped by one's father.
phrases.notes: These words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא דָּיְיקַתְּ מַתְנִיתִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי meant that לוי should have noticed that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids אנוסת אביו.

steps.title: Proof from the next mishnah: what does 'his mother' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes the next משנה about six more severe women and asks why it lists both 'his mother' and 'his father's wife.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it teaches: Six forbidden women are more severe than these, because they are married to others, so their rival wives are permitted: his mother, his father's wife, and his father's sister. What is 'his mother'? If you say she is married to his father, that is the same as 'his father's wife'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts proving that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. He quotes the next משנה and shows that 'his mother' cannot mean a mother married to his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next משנה lists six women who are forbidden even more strictly. If 'his mother' meant his father's wife, it would be a repeat of 'his father's wife,' and the list would not reach six. So 'his mother' must mean something else, which the next step will spell out.

keyTerms.meaning: More severe forbidden relationships
Their rival wives (other wives of the same husband)
If you say
That is the same as

phrases.english: As it teaches:
Six forbidden women are more severe than these,
phrases.notes: This is the next משנה. 'These' means the fifteen women listed in the first משנה.

phrases.english: because they are married to others,
their rival wives are permitted:
his mother, his father's wife, and his father's sister.
What is "his mother"?
If you say she is married to his father,
that is the same as "his father's wife"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for the claim of step 8 that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The next משנה, listing 'his mother' separately from 'his father's wife'

steps.title: So 'his mother' is a woman raped by his father, which is רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: 'His mother' must mean a woman his father raped. The משנה treats her as forbidden to all the brothers, which only רבי יהודה holds, so she was left out of the first list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean a woman raped by his father. And it teaches: 'because they are married to others,' which means to others yes, to the brothers no. Whom have you heard who holds this view? רבי יהודה, who forbids a woman raped by one's father. That is why the first משנה did not list her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes the proof. 'His mother' is a woman his father raped, and the משנה says she can marry only outsiders, never any brother, which matches רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'married to others' tell us that none of the brothers could ever marry her. That only makes sense if a woman raped by one's father is forbidden to every son of that father, and that is רבי יהודה's view. Since she belongs in the 'six severe' list, the first משנה had no reason to list her, which answers לוי's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (it must be)
To the brothers, no
A view or line of reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רבי does not hold of רבי חייא's rules. The woman raped by one's father is missing from the first משנה because the משניות follow רבי יהודה, who forbids her to all the brothers, so she belongs in the list of the six more severe women.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'his mother' in the second משנה means a woman married to his father. That would repeat 'his father's wife.' Here 'his mother' means a woman his father raped.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not one raped by his father?
And it teaches: because they are married to others:
to others, yes; to the brothers, no.
Whom have you heard
who holds this view?
Rabbi Yehuda, who forbids a woman raped by one's father.
That is why he did not teach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 9 and closes רב אשי's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids אנוסת אביו to all the brothers, so she appears among the six severe women and was rightly left out of the first list.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה could have a case where she falls to her son
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי: even according to רבי יהודה, אנוסת אביו could fall before her son if one of the brothers broke the rule and married her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Even according to רבי יהודה you can find this case, where a brother broke the rule and married her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אשי's explanation from Step 10. He shows a way that אנוסת אביו could still fall to her son for ייבום, even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the משנה left her out because, according to רבי יהודה, she can never reach her son. רבינא answers that if a paternal brother broke the rule and married her anyway, the marriage would still take effect. If that brother then died without children, she would fall to her son. So she could have been listed after all.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it, meaning a real case exists
Also, too
He went against the rule and married her anyway

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Even according to Rabbi Yehuda, you can find this case
if a brother broke the rule and married her!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that, according to רבי יהודה, אנוסת אביו can never come before her son for ייבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A brother who wrongly married her creates a valid marriage. When he dies, she falls to her son, so she could have been listed in the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה does not list cases that need wrongdoing
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה does not teach 'what if someone sinned' cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה does not teach cases of 'if he did it anyway.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבינא's challenge. The משנה only lists cases that can happen without anyone breaking a rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's case only works if a brother sinned by marrying a forbidden woman. The משנה's list does not include situations that depend on sinning first. So רב אשי's explanation still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If': here, a case that only happens if someone broke a rule
It teaches (said about the משנה)

phrases.english: The Mishna does not teach 'what if' cases.
phrases.notes: 'What if' cases are cases that only come about because someone broke a rule first.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה's scope: it does not list cases that depend on a sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any possible case, even one that comes from a forbidden marriage, should appear in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only cases that can happen without anyone sinning.

steps.title: A case with no forbidden marriage: יעקב and his daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי suggests a case without 'if': a father rapes his son's wife and has a son with her. The husband dies childless, and she falls to her own son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: Even without an 'if' case you can find it. יעקב raped his daughter-in-law and had a son with her. Then her husband ראובן died without children. She falls before her own son, and since she is forbidden to him, her צרה is forbidden too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new case where nobody married wrongly. In this case, even according to רבי יהודה, אנוסת אביו falls before her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראובן's marriage to her was fully allowed, so Step 12's answer about wrongdoing does not apply. Her son by יעקב is ראובן's paternal brother, so she falls to him for ייבום. She is forbidden to him as his mother, so her צרה is forbidden as well. That means she could have been listed in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced, raped
His daughter-in-law (his son's wife)
Since, because of the fact that
A co-wife: another wife of the same husband

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
Even without a 'what if' case, you can find it:
Yaakov raped his daughter-in-law
and fathered a son from her,
and Reuven died without children.
phrases.notes: ראובן is יעקב's son, her husband. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: So she falls before her own son for yibum,
phrases.notes: Her son by יעקב is ראובן's brother from the same father, so he is one of the brothers she falls to.

phrases.english: and since she herself is forbidden to him,
her co-wife is also forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around Step 12's answer by building a case with no forbidden marriage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, according to רבי יהודה, the משנה could not include אנוסת אביו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rape by the father followed by a fully allowed marriage still brings her before her son, with no 'if' needed.

steps.title: The משנה deals only with legitimate siblings
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the משנה only deals with brothers born from permitted relationships. A son from a forbidden relationship is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The משנה deals with siblings from a permitted relationship. It does not deal with siblings from a forbidden relationship.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא rejects רב אשי's יעקב case. The son in that case was born from a forbidden relationship, and the משנה does not deal with such cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child born when a father has relations with his daughter-in-law is a ממזר. The משנה's cases of ייבום are built only on siblings from permitted relationships. So the יעקב case is outside the משנה's scope, and leaving out אנוסת אביו still makes sense according to רבי יהודה.

Forbidden

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the משנה's cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any family relationship, even one created by a forbidden act, counts for the משנה's list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only deals with siblings born from permitted relationships, so the יעקב case does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list leaves out cases that depend on a forbidden marriage (Step 12) and cases that depend on a ממזר brother (Step 14). That is why, according to רבי יהודה, אנוסת אביו does not appear in it.

steps.title: Even so, לוי included this case in his collection
steps.stepSummary: Even though רבי criticized him, לוי did include this kind of case in his own collection of teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, לוי included it in his collection of teachings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that לוי, despite everything said so far, put this kind of case into his own collection. This sets up the quote from לוי's ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי scolded לוי for wanting to add this case. Here we learn that לוי still taught it in his own ברייתא. The next step quotes that ברייתא as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: And even so, nevertheless

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the back-and-forth to a report about לוי's own teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי included the case of 'his mother' (including אנוסת אביו) in his own ברייתא.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא: sometimes his mother exempts her צרה and sometimes not
steps.stepSummary: לוי taught that 'his mother' sometimes exempts her צרה and sometimes does not. The first example given is a case where she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As לוי taught: His mother sometimes exempts her צרה and sometimes does not. How so? If his mother was married to his father, and then she married his paternal brother, and that brother died, this is 'his mother who does not exempt her צרה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes לוי's ברייתא to show that he included 'his mother' in his list. It starts with the example where she does not exempt her צרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After his father died, his mother married his paternal brother. That is marrying a brother's wife, which is punishable by כרת, so the marriage never takes effect. Since she was never really the brother's wife, she does not exempt the other wife, and that other wife can do ייבום with the son.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, releases from ייבום
How so? (opens an explanation)
His brother from the same father

steps.confusionAlert: In this case 'his mother' does NOT exempt her צרה. That is because her marriage to his brother never took effect, not because she is allowed to him. She is still forbidden to her son.
